title.en: Collapsed glacier likely caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, scientists say
title.zh: 科学家称，冰川崩塌可能是尼泊尔-西藏毁灭性洪灾的原因

summary.en: Preliminary investigations by scientists have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice.
summary.zh: 科学家初步调查指出，冰川崩塌是此次洪灾的原因，凸显了喜马拉雅冰川迅速融化的问题。

body.en:
Preliminary investigations have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause of the flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice, scientists have told the BBC.

Initial reports of an earthquake led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the flood that has killed at least 469 people.

However, the US Geological Survey then clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.

Dr Simon Cook, a glacier expert with the University of Dundee, told the BBC his team had detected that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - which is approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.

He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a northwesterly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

An analysis , external by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), an intergovernmental scientific institution, found there could have been "an ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-altitude area".

This caused a "large volume of ice and rock debris" to enter the Lende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi river, which in turn generated a sudden surge in the river carrying water, sediment and large boulders downstream.

The centre found that water levels in rivers downstream rose by between seven and nine metres within a span of 30 minutes, and several water monitoring stations were washed away or damaged.

Mike Searle, a professor of earth sciences at Oxford University, said that this whole process - from landslide to flood - could have taken hours or even days.

"The sheer wave of debris suggests there could have been a landslide first; the water built up, dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The topography of the area could have also exacerbated the flood. Searle pointed out that Langtang Lirung sits on the crest of the high Himalayas and there are "incredibly steep valleys" on both sides of the mountain, which could have funnelled the water at higher speeds.

Searle said that Langtang Lirung, like the rest of the Himalayas, has been slowly rising due to long-term tectonic movement, where one plate has been pushing another plate up. "It's like putting a jack under the car, and then jacking it up."

"As the mountain is rising, the glacier gets steeper and steeper, and it's inevitable that parts of it fall off."

body.zh: 科学家告诉英国广播公司，初步调查表明，尼泊尔和西藏边境山洪爆发的原因是冰川崩塌，这凸显了喜马拉雅冰川迅速融化的问题。 最初的地震报告让许多人相信地震引发了山体滑坡，进而引发了洪水，造成至少 469 人死亡。 然而，美国地质调查局随后澄清，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 根据美国地质勘探局的数据和分析该事件的科学家的数据，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级。 邓迪大学冰川专家西蒙·库克博士告诉英国广播公司，他的团队发现尼泊尔朗塘利龙峰附近的冰川下部已经崩塌，该峰位于洪水所在地以西约 15 公里（9 英里）处。 他估计冰川向西北方向崩塌，然后向下游向西移动。 政府间科学机构国际山地综合开发中心（ICIMOD）的一项外部分析发现，可能存在“源自高海拔地区的冰岩雪崩”。 这导致“大量冰和岩石碎片”进入博特科希河的支流伦德科拉河，进而导致河水突然激增，将水、沉积物和大石块带到下游。 该中心发现，下游河流水位在30分钟内上涨了7至9米，多个水监测站被冲毁或损坏。 牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，从山体滑坡到洪水的整个过程可能需要数小时甚至数天。 他告诉英国广播公司：“巨大的碎片浪潮表明，可能首先发生了山体滑坡；水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后爆发了一场巨大的洪水。” 该地区的地形也可能加剧洪水。塞尔指出，Langtang Lirung 坐落在喜马拉雅山的山顶，山的两侧都有“极其陡峭的山谷”，这可能会导致水以更高的速度流入。 塞尔表示，Langtang Lirung 与喜马拉雅山的其他地区一样，由于长期的构造运动，一个板块一直在推动另一个板块上升，一直在缓慢上升。 “这就像在汽车下面放一个千斤顶，然后把它顶起来。” “随着山的上升，冰川变得越来越陡，部分冰川脱落是不可避免的。” 但通常这些都是较小的块，会暂时堵塞河流，并且很容易......

In moments of such profound loss and environmental tragedy, our hearts ache for those who mourn. Revelation 21:4 offers a future hope where Yahweh himself will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境的毁灭性洪灾，据称由冰川崩塌引起，夺走了至少469人的生命，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此深重的损失和环境悲剧中，我们的心为那些哀悼的人而痛。启示录21:4提供了一个未来的盼望，雅伟自己将擦去所有的眼泪，不再有死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: 'The flood took everything': Nepal survivors describe horror of loved ones being swept away
title.zh: “洪水夺走了一切”：尼泊尔幸存者描述亲人被冲走的恐惧

summary.en: One woman says her father, mother, sister and sister's children were carried away before her eyes.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Survivors of massive flash floods in Nepal have recounted how they saw their loved ones disappear into torrents of mud.

At least 469 people have died and several hundred others are missing after floods wiped out entire villages on the border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, with a force so powerful seismologists initially identified it as an earthquake.

Rescuers trudged through thick mud and debris on Thursday as Nepalese authorities rushed to bring aid and relief supplies to the affected areas.

"My family members were swept away by the flood in front of my eyes," Kalpana Malla from Nepal's Nuwakot district told the BBC.

Malla said her father, mother, sister and sister's children were all claimed by the disaster.

"They could not escape the flood; there was no chance at all," she said. "This flood took everything, but my son and I climbed the rooftop of a house and survived but couldn't explain how."

He said he had given his phone to his sister so she could keep in touch, but the mobile was no longer reachable.

Another woman, Goma Pandit, said she had lost her buffaloes and all her other cattle.

"My farmland is also swept away. Ten sacks of mustard seeds, tons of corn and rice paddy are all gone. Nothing is left."

At Kathmandu's TU Teaching Hospital, families of those missing in the floods wait anxiously for updates.

Holding up her phone, Ram Khumari Shrestha says: "This is my husband. He was off to Rasuwa as a part of his driving job. He was in contact with me until 8 pm yesterday.

"But I couldn't call him this morning. The phone was switched off," she told the BBC.

Mani Shrestha Bishwa was also camped out at the hospital on Wednesday night, hoping to hear from his younger brother, cousin, uncle and friend.

Trekking guide Sonam Dorjee missed the flood in his home village of Rasiwa Syafru by about an hour. He had left at 08:00 local time.

As he was driving to Kathmandu, Dorjee told the BBC he had heard the sound of floods gushing into their village.

"It [sounded] like an earthquake," he said. "My house has collapsed... I have seen a photo."

Dorjee said his sister, Dechen Tamang, was missing, along with her husband and several other family members.

"Many survivors are now left without homes and they need emergency rescue and evacuation, as well as food, temporary accommodation and medical support."

He is praying his sister is found alive. "There is a 10% chance, we hope," he said.
body.zh: 尼泊尔大规模山洪爆发的幸存者讲述了他们如何看到亲人消失在泥浆洪流中。 周三，洪水摧毁了尼泊尔和西藏边境的整个村庄，造成至少 469 人死亡，数百人失踪，其威力如此强大，地震学家最初将其确定为地震。 周四，尼泊尔当局紧急向受影响地区运送援助和救灾物资，救援人员艰难地穿过厚厚的泥浆和废墟。 来自尼泊尔努瓦科特地区的卡尔帕纳·马拉告诉英国广播公司：“我的家人在我眼前被洪水冲走。” 马拉说，她的父亲、母亲、姐姐和姐姐的孩子都在这场灾难中丧生。 “他们无法逃离洪水；根本没有机会，”她说。 “这场洪水夺走了一切，但我和儿子爬上了屋顶，活了下来，但无法解释如何活下来。” 他说，他已将手机交给了妹妹，以便她能保持联系，但手机已无法接通。 另一位名叫戈马·潘迪特的妇女说，她失去了她的水牛和所有其他牛。 “我的田地也被冲走了，十袋芥菜籽、成吨的玉米、稻田都没有了，什么都没有了。” 在加德满都的工业大学教学医院，洪水中失踪人员的家人焦急地等待最新消息。 拉姆·库马里·什雷斯塔 (Ram Khumari Shrestha) 举起手机说道：“这是我的丈夫。他去拉苏瓦是为了完成驾驶工作。昨天晚上 8 点之前他一直与我联系。” “但今天早上我无法给他打电话。电话已关机，”她告诉英国广播公司。 周三晚上，马尼·什雷斯塔·比什瓦 (Mani Shrestha Bishwa) 也在医院露营，希望听到他弟弟、表弟、叔叔和朋友的消息。 徒步向导索南·多吉 (Sonam Dorjee) 比家乡拉西瓦·沙夫鲁 (Rasiwa Syafru) 的洪水晚了大约一个小时。他于当地时间08:00离开。 当多吉开车前往加德满都时，他告诉英国广播公司，他听到洪水涌入他们村庄的声音。 “这（听起来）就像一场地震，”他说。 “我的房子倒塌了……我看过照片。” 多吉说，他的妹妹德钦·塔芒（Dechen Tamang）、她的丈夫和其他几名家庭成员失踪了。 “许多幸存者现在无家可归，他们需要紧急救援和疏散，以及食物、临时住宿和医疗支持。” 他正在祈祷他的妹妹还活着。 “我们希望有 10% 的机会，”他说。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: How this 30m tunnel became the centre of a growing border dispute
title.zh: 这条 30m 长的隧道如何成为日益严重的边界争端的中心

summary.en: The latest escalation in tensions between Latvia and Belarus was found hidden among trees and bushes at a border crossing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Latvia's border guard has accused Belarusian authorities of partial responsibility for a recently discovered migrant tunnel beneath a border fence between the two nations.

The tunnel was uncovered by Latvian authorities in early August. Latvia faces an increasing number of migrants trying to cross the border from Belarus, further straining relations between the two countries.

Latvia shares a 173km border with Belarus. Latvia is a member of the European Union. Belarus, an independent nation with an authoritarian government, is not.

At the time of the tunnel's discovery, Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said criminal networks were facilitating migration from Belarus into Latvia, bringing migrants into Europe's borderless Schengen area, but that the migrants' final destination was elsewhere on the continent.

"They migrate to where it's easier (to enter the EU). So we must not be the easiest place," Kulbergs told the press conference.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

He pledged to target networks transporting the migrants from the border to their destinations, as well as any support points for migrants in Latvia, as part of what he called "Operation Werewolf".

"If everything goes according to plan, we are confident that we will already deal a serious enough blow to the system," Kulbergs said. "I want to tell the organisers: everything will be put to an end."

Latvia's government said in a statement it would cooperate with neighbours Estonia, Lithuania, Poland and others to stop the flow of migrants.

Latvia, along with Lithuania and Poland, has frequently accused Belarus' authoritarian government of smuggling migrants from crisis-impacted regions close to the EU's far borders.

Having now discovered a second tunnel at another point along the border fence, Latvia is pointing fingers at the Belarusian border guard.

"It is simply impossible to build such a tunnel without the Belarusian border guards being aware of it," Guntis Pujats, head of the agency, told Latvian radio on Thursday.

Pujats went on to give more information about the original tunnel, saying that the entrance on the Belarusian side of the border was found around 10m from the border line and had been hidden among trees and bushes. The tunnel itself was reported to be 80cm wide and to run for roughly 30m.

Some 28 cubic metres of earth had been removed to construct the tunnel. Support structures had been erected within the tunnel to keep it from collapsing, and a plywood cover had been fitted to the entrance.

"The construction work was quite extensive. So the relevant authorities were undoubtedly aware of it," he said.

body.zh: 拉脱维亚边防部队指责白俄罗斯当局对最近在两国边境围栏下发现的移民隧道负有部分责任。 拉脱维亚当局于八月初发现了这条隧道。拉脱维亚面临越来越多试图从白俄罗斯越境的移民，这进一步加剧了两国关系的紧张。 拉脱维亚与白俄罗斯有 173 公里的边界。拉脱维亚是欧盟成员。白俄罗斯是一个拥有独裁政府的独立国家，但事实并非如此。 在隧道被发现时，拉脱维亚总理安德里斯·库尔伯格斯表示，犯罪网络正在为从白俄罗斯到拉脱维亚的移民提供便利，将移民带入欧洲无边界的申根区，但移民的最终目的地是欧洲大陆的其他地方。 “他们移民到更容易（进入欧盟）的地方。所以我们一定不是最容易的地方，”库尔伯格在新闻发布会上说。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 他承诺将打击将移民从边境运送到目的地的网络，以及拉脱维亚境内为移民提供的任何支持点，作为他所谓的“狼人行动”的一部分。 库尔伯格说：“如果一切按计划进行，我们相信我们已经对系统造成了足够严重的打击。” “我想告诉组织者：一切都会结束。” 拉脱维亚政府在一份声明中表示，将与邻国爱沙尼亚、立陶宛、波兰等国合作阻止移民流动。 拉脱维亚、立陶宛和波兰经常指责白俄罗斯独裁政府从靠近欧盟边境的受危机影响的地区偷运移民。 现在，拉脱维亚在边境围栏的另一处发现了第二条隧道，并将矛头指向白俄罗斯边防部队。 该机构负责人冈蒂斯·普贾茨周四对拉脱维亚电台表示：“在白俄罗斯边防部队不知情的情况下，根本不可能修建这样的隧道。” Pujats接着提供了有关原始隧道的更多信息，称边界白俄罗斯一侧的入口距离边界线约10m，隐藏在树木和灌木丛中。据报道，隧道本身宽 80 厘米，长约 30 m。 为了建造隧道，已拆除了约 28 立方米的土方。隧道内已竖立支撑结构以防止其倒塌，入口处已安装胶合板盖。 “建设工作相当广泛。所以相关部门无疑是意识到这一点的，”他说。 Pujats声称12条地下隧道已被...

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 我们对尼泊尔和西藏致命洪水的了解

summary.en: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Massive landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.

Search and rescue operations are continuing after Wednesday's disaster. Chinese state media has said there are significant casualties, while Nepalese officials describe "huge scale loss".

But rescuers are on edge because of the risk of further flooding. A lake of rising water has formed at a site along the border, and Chinese state media says it is at "high risk" of bursting its banks.

Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating flood.

However, the US Geological Survey has clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.

Debris flow from the collapse "caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream" the USGS said.

Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region. Scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events as rescue efforts continue.

Geologist Daniel Shugar – one of the first experts to suggest Wednesday's flash flooding event could have been caused by glacial activity – says glacial thinning inducted by global warming can increase the risk of landslides.

But it is still too early to definitively link the event to climate change, Shugar, who is based at the University of Calgary in Canada, tells the BBC.

Simon Cook, a geoscientist at the University of Dundee, says however, that climate change "could have an impact". Cook added that his team believed they had identified where the collapse had occured. He told the BBC that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.

He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a north-westerly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

He told the BBC "permafrost is partially holding some mountainsides together, this permafrost is warming and thawing and degrading so you are going to get more landslides".

Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

He told the BBC: "I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, (which) dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood."

body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境的大规模山体滑坡和山洪造成大范围破坏，造成数百人死亡或失踪。 周三灾难发生后，搜救行动仍在继续。中国官方媒体称造成重大人员伤亡，而尼泊尔官员则形容“损失规模巨大”。 但由于洪水进一步泛滥的风险，救援人员感到紧张。边境一处水位不断上涨，形成了一个湖泊，中国官方媒体称，该湖面临决堤的“高风险”。 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生地震的最初报道让许多人相信地震导致了山体滑坡，进而引发了毁灭性的洪水。 然而，美国地质调查局澄清，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 根据美国地质勘探局的数据和分析该事件的科学家的数据，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级。 美国地质调查局表示，塌方产生的泥石流“对下游造成了随后的灾难性影响”。 众所周知，气候变化正在加速兴都库什喜马拉雅地区的冰川融化。随着救援工作的继续，科学家们正试图拼凑出事件的确切顺序。 地质学家丹尼尔·舒加尔（Daniel Shugar）是最早提出周三山洪爆发可能是由冰川活动引起的专家之一，他表示，全球变暖导致的冰川变薄会增加山体滑坡的风险。 但目前将这一事件与气候变化联系起来还为时过早，加拿大卡尔加里大学的舒加尔告诉英国广播公司。 然而，邓迪大学地球科学家西蒙·库克表示，气候变化“可能会产生影响”。库克补充说，他的团队相信他们已经确定了倒塌发生的位置。他告诉 BBC，尼泊尔 Langtang Lirung 峰附近的冰川下部（洪水发生地以西约 15 公里（9 英里）处）已经崩塌。 他估计冰川向西北方向崩塌，然后向下游向西移动。 他告诉英国广播公司“永久冻土部分将一些山坡固定在一起，永久冻土正在变暖、融化和退化，因此将会发生更多的山体滑坡”。 牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，在洪水袭击尼泊尔和西藏之前“几小时或几天”，冰川可能已经崩塌。 他告诉英国广播公司：“我认为，巨大的碎片浪潮表明首先发生了山体滑坡，水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后在一场巨大的洪水中决堤。” 一种可能性是降雨或融冰产生的水可能破坏了地面或冰的稳定性，......

title.en: France's cheese makers are confronting a problem tradition alone can't solve
title.zh: 法国奶酪制造商正面临传统无法解决的问题

summary.en: France's local cheeses, a source of national pride, are under threat as climate change forces authorities to relax strict production rules for varieties like Abondance and Beaufort due to severe drought.
summary.zh: 法国当地奶酪是国家的骄傲，但由于气候变化引发的严重干旱，当局不得不放宽对 Abondance 和 Beaufort 等品种的严格生产规定。

body.en:
Widespread drought and record-breaking heatwaves have forced France to relax some of its famously strict rules on cheese production, with authorities announcing special measures for abondance, beaufort and comte.

France's vast array of local cheeses are a source of national pride, and authorities go to great lengths to protect traditional production methods and ensure authenticity.

To earn a coveted "appellation d'origine protegee" (Protected Designation of Origin) label — and the right to give their cheese a particular protected name — producers must follow rigid rules on where their animals graze and what they eat.

But the summer's drought, which affected 95 per cent of mainland France in July, has left normally rich pastures dry and bare.

In response, the government said this week that producers of abondance, beaufort and comte, hard cheeses made from the raw milk of cows grazing in the Alps and Jura mountains, can supplement the animals' diet with more fodder and grain brought in from elsewhere.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Growth on permanent grasslands as of 10 August is a third less than the 1989-2018 average, according to the agriculture ministry's statistical service.

The fodder situation is "highly degraded" in almost all regions, the ministry said earlier this month.

The National Institute of Origin and Quality (INAO), the government agency that administers and enforces rules of origin, says it will also grant temporary relief for several other cheeses including reblochon, cantal, bleu d'Auvergne, and fourme d'Ambert.

Europe's record-breaking summer heat has caused thousands of excess deaths, set wildfires blazing and seen major rivers drop to record lows.

In France, farmers are bracing for their smallest corn crop since 1980, and winegrowers are reporting some of the earliest harvests on record.

Scientists say human-caused climate change has intensified the drought, with extreme heat rather than low rainfall driving the dry conditions.

title.en: Protesters set fire to migrant camp in Ceuta
title.zh: 抗议者纵火焚烧休达的移民营地

summary.en: The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.

Protesters in Ceuta set fire to a migrant camp and clashed with police on Thursday. The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish enclave in North Africa.

Footage on Spanish television showed a group of demonstrators on a beach, throwing objects into the fire. Police pushed the protesters back while the migrants retreated to a pier.

Earlier on Thursday, a military vehicle was attacked with stones and other objects by about 70 people, a police spokesman in Ceuta told the AFP news agency.

Local protesters tried to stop Red Cross vehicles from reaching the beach to distribute food to migrants. People waving Spanish flags shouted "They should leave" and "Out with the Red Cross."

In July, more than 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta irregularly in the hope of reaching the European mainland.

While the vast majority of them have since returned to Morocco, several thousand remain in Ceuta , living on the streets or on the beach.

Spain's government in Madrid puts the number at below 7,000 while Ceuta officials say it's at least 10,000. Ceuta's population is about 84,000 people. 

The Spanish government is under growing pressure over the situation in Ceuta. The conservative opposition is accusing left-wing Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of failing to act and abandoning Ceuta's residents.

Madrid has recently moved to speed up efforts to identify the migrants and decide who will be sent back to Morocco. The government also approved extra funding to help unaccompanied minors entitled to special protection . 

The crisis comes ahead of general elections next year and has deepened political divisions in Spain. The conservative opposition is calling for a tougher stance on migration.

The mass influx in July had also led to tension within the EU over how to respond to the situation in Ceuta.

title.en: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America
title.zh: 特朗普签署命令将安大略湖更名为美国湖

summary.en: Trump's order comes after the trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed late last week.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America.

The move comes after trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed late last week, and the US imposed new 50% tariffs on $20bn (C$28bn) worth of Canadian goods. Canada will implement "dollar for dollar" counter tariffs next month.

Trump has repeatedly posted threats about renaming the lake, one of the five Great Lakes that straddle both countries, on social media amid the trade dispute.

He said on Thursday the move was "official, effective immediately" and that his administration has "filed all the necessary papers, documents" to make the change.

Text of the executive order says it gives the US Department of the Interior 30 days to update the name change with the Geographic Names Information Service - the official repository of domestic geographic names in the US.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted the name Lake Ontario can be traced back more than 400 years, adding in a social media post on Thursday that preceded the formation of the Canadian Confederation and the US Declaration of Independence.

"We know that the United States is changing. Their trade relations, their foreign policy, their national monuments, their hydronyms," he wrote. "Canadian women and men also know that things must be called by their name, and this lake is called Lake Ontario – today and forever."

When Trump took the White House in 2025, he signed a similar order that changed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Mexico has rejected the name change, arguing a single country cannot rename a shared body of international water.

It also led to a legal dispute between Mexico and tech giant Google, which renamed the gulf in its maps application. , external

In that case, Google Maps users in the US see "Gulf of America", while those in Mexico see the "Gulf of Mexico". Those in other countries see the "Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America)".

The White House at the time also blocked Associated Press reporters from presidential events over the news agency's refusal to adopt the name "Gulf of America" in its coverage. The AP sued the Trump administration in response, and that legal battle is ongoing.

There is no universally recognised international body setting the names of international waters. While the US president has broad discretion over how his country officially recognises landmarks, other countries do not have to follow.

Canada does not have to recognise name changes made by other countries and officials there have dismissed the idea.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote on social media, "It's Lake Ontario to Canadians and the rest of the world. Now and forever."

Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston agreed, saying "We're into some real foolishness now....

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has stepped up an escalating feud with Canada, ordering that Lake Ontario — a body of water shared by both countries — be renamed "Lake America".

Trump signed an executive order on the name change at the White House on Friday, as the North American neighbours plunge deeper into a trade war .

"We're going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

Behind Trump's desk were two maps of the US-Canada border — one with the words "Lake America" in red over the lake, and the other with the header "Making the Great Lakes Even Greater".

Asked why he was targeting an ally for punishment instead of US adversaries, Trump replied: "The Canadian officials have treated us very badly. They're nasty people."

"People, oftentimes, they'll ask me who's the worst to deal with on trade? And I said that's easy. Canada. They are the worst to trade with," the 80-year-old Republican added.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pushed back against Trump's renaming of Lake Ontario, citing the name's indigenous origins, as the row between the neighbours roiled on.

"We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms," Carney said in a post on X.

"Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario — then, now and always."

US-Canada trade talks collapsed at the eleventh hour last week, with Trump's tariffs taking effect on Saturday.

Canada responded with tit-for-tat tariffs on Wednesday, with Carney saying: "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked."

The same day, Trump announced that he was giving "serious consideration" to changing the name to Lake America, later posting a TikTok video saying he intended to do so.

The name change mirrors Trump's unilateral altering of the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on his first day back in office in January 2025.

That change obliged the US federal government to refer to the gulf by the new designation, although Mexico has rejected any move to rename it and it lacks international recognition.

Trump said the name change was "something I've been thinking about for a long time".

"As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico, we changed it, and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America."

"So, if you think about it, we have a gulf and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean. So, maybe we'll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we'll change them both," he said.

title.en: Nepal's glacier collapse sends a warning beyond the Himalayas
title.zh: 尼泊尔冰川崩塌向喜马拉雅山以外地区发出警告

summary.en: Nepal's glacier collapse has exposed a growing risk, highlighting how other glacial regions such as New Zealand could face similar threats.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The catastrophic glacier collapse that devastated communities on the Nepal-Tibet border has highlighted a growing danger facing mountain regions around the world, as climate change alters the frozen landscapes that help hold them together.

Raising a bigger question: as the world warms, are other mountain regions becoming more vulnerable to disasters like this?

Scientists say it is too early to say global warming directly caused this week's disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border.

But rising temperatures are changing glaciers, snow and permafrost in ways that can make some high-altitude slopes increasingly unstable, potentially increasing the risk of catastrophic collapses, landslides and floods.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

New Zealand's Southern Alps have many of the same physical features, including glaciers, steep mountain faces, ice and snow, and valleys where a sudden collapse could send huge amounts of rock, ice and water downstream.

The country's exposure is different from Nepal's, with far fewer people living in its highest mountain areas.

Preliminary analysis suggests a large mass of ice and rock collapsed from the slopes of Langtang Lirung, a mountain rising more than 7,000 metres above sea level.

The debris crashed into the Lhende Khola river, generating a huge surge of water, sediment and boulders that tore downstream.

One possibility is that the collapse temporarily blocked the river, creating a natural dam before the backed-up water burst through.

Water levels downstream rose by as much as nine metres in just 30 minutes, experts told AAP.

The sheer force of the collapse was initially mistaken for an earthquake after seismic instruments detected a magnitude 5.2 signal.

But scientists later determined the seismic energy was generated by the glacier collapse itself.

Mountain environments are naturally dynamic, particularly in a region as tectonically active as the Himalayas, meaning earthquakes, heavy rainfall, snow and the natural movement of glaciers can all trigger collapses.

But climate change can alter the conditions that determine how stable those systems are.

Experts urge that as temperatures rise, glaciers retreat and lose ice, which causes ice to act as a buttress, helping support steep mountain slopes.

When it disappears, previously ice-covered rock is exposed to warmer temperatures, rainfall and repeated cycles of freezing and thawing.

And permafrost, ground that has remained frozen for years, can thaw, removing another source of stability.

body.en:
The fate of US mother Lindsay Clancy is now in the hands of a Massachusetts jury, who must decide if she is guilty of first-degree murder - the intentional and premeditated killing of another person - in the deaths of her three children.

For five weeks, the trial has gripped the country as Clancy's lawyers have argued that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis when she killed her children, who ranged in age from eight months to five years. Clancy does not deny killing her two sons and daughter.

The prosecution argued she made a calculated decision to intentionally murder them.

The jury could find Clancy guilty of first-degree murder, guilty of lesser charges, or not guilty.

The jury of nine women and three men completed their first day of deliberations on Thursday. They will return on Friday.

In the state of Massachusetts, a first-degree murder conviction carries a mandatory life in prison sentence without the possibility of parole.

The jury could instead find Clancy guilty of second-degree murder - committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without prior planning - or involuntary manslaughter - causing death because of extreme carelessness. Those convictions, too, would lead to some prison time.

If Clancy is found not guilty by reason of insanity, then she will not be set free, but instead sent to a psychiatric hospital, where she possibly could remain for life.

Attorneys for both sides made closing arguments on Thursday before the jury began deliberating.

Kevin Reddington, Clancy's lawyer, repeated the defence's argument that she was experiencing postpartum psychosis when she killed the children with exercise bands at their home and then attempted to end her own life by jumping out of a window. Clancy was paralysed by the attempt and has attended the trial in a wheelchair.

"This young lady is not guilty of the killing of her children because she was suffering from a disease and defect," Reddington said, adding that he believed prosecutors were "not going to be able to prove otherwise".

The UK's National Health Service (NHS) defines postpartum psychosis as a rare and serious mental health illness that can affect someone soon after having a baby, and which should be treated as a medical emergency.

One of the more tense moments of the closing arguments came when Reddington directly addressed the prosecutors and asked them to explain why they tried to prove Clancy's suicide attempt was not serious. The judge interrupted and ordered him to address only the jury.

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague did not dispute that Clancy was mentally ill, but told the jury that the defendant could tell the difference between right and wrong at the time of the killings.

body.zh: 美国母亲林赛·克兰西的命运现在掌握在马萨诸塞州陪审团的手中，陪审团必须决定她是否犯有一级谋杀罪，即故意和有预谋地杀害另一个人，导致她的三个孩子死亡。 五周以来，该审判一直困扰着全国，克兰西的律师辩称，她在杀死八个月至五岁的孩子时患有产后精神病。克兰西并不否认杀害了她的两个儿子和女儿。 检方辩称，她做出了故意谋杀他们的深思熟虑的决定。 陪审团可能会裁定克兰西犯有一级谋杀罪、犯有较轻的罪名或无罪。 由九名女性和三名男性组成的陪审团于周四完成了第一天的审议。他们将于周五返回。 在马萨诸塞州，一级谋杀罪将被判处终身监禁，不得假释。 相反，陪审团可能会裁定克兰西犯有二级谋杀罪——恶意或极端鲁莽，但没有事先计划——或非自愿过失杀人——因极度粗心而导致死亡。这些定罪也会导致入狱。 如果克兰西因精神错乱而被判无罪，那么她将不会被释放，而是会被送往精神病院，她可能会终生留在那里。 周四，在陪审团开始审议之前，双方律师均进行了结案陈词。 克兰西的律师凯文·雷丁顿（Kevin Reddington）重申了辩方的论点，即她在家中用健身带杀死了孩子们，然后试图跳出窗户结束自己的生命，当时她正在经历产后精神病。克兰西因这次尝试而瘫痪，并坐在轮椅上参加了审判。 雷丁顿说：“这位年轻的女士没有杀害她的孩子的罪名，因为她患有疾病和缺陷，”他补充说，他相信检察官“无法证明其他情况”。 英国国家医疗服务体系 (NHS) 将产后精神病定义为一种罕见且严重的精神健康疾病，可能会在产后不久影响某人，应将其视为医疗紧急情况。 结案陈词中最紧张的时刻之一是雷丁顿直接向检察官讲话，要求他们解释为什么他们试图证明克兰西的自杀企图并不严重。法官打断了他的话，命令他只向陪审团发表讲话。 检察官詹妮弗·斯普拉格没有否认克兰西患有精神疾病，但告诉陪审团，被告在杀人时可以辨别是非。 “这不是系统或 DSM 导致她勒死她的孩子，”......

title.en: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
title.zh: 西班牙：窃贼在维耶纳博物馆的闪电袭击中窃取了青铜时代的黄金

summary.en: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 世界上最伟大的青铜时代黄金藏品之一几乎全部被从维耶纳博物馆盗走。一群高度专业的窃贼在博物馆开放前四分钟内就进进出出。 周四，窃贼袭击了世界上最伟大的青铜时代黄金藏品之一，这是近几个月来欧洲博物馆发生的一系列引人注目的抢劫案中的最新一起。 清晨对西班牙东部维耶纳博物馆的袭击只持续了几分钟。 一名官员称，一群窃贼“速度超快、超专业”，几乎盗走了维耶纳的整个宝藏藏品，只留下了一些物品。 镇议会发言人说：“维耶纳博物馆的警报于凌晨 5 点 20 分左右响起。”他补充说，四分钟之内，他们就以极其迅速和专业的行动再次离开了大楼。 青铜时代的黄金藏品（我们现在知道其中一些来自陨石）是阿利坎特省小型博物馆的核心展品。 “他们拿走了大部分财宝，”维耶纳市长 Fulgencio Cerdan 告诉记者。 “我们完全被摧毁了，我什至在颤抖。事实是，对于我们这些来自维耶纳的人来说，这摧毁了我们。这是我们遗产、我们财富的一部分。” 西班牙政府驻阿利坎特副代表曼努埃尔·皮内达 (Manuel Pineda) 表示，窃贼乘坐几辆车抵达，显然是“通过窗户”进入博物馆的。 塞尔丹市长表示，藏品中只剩下三件银器、一只手镯、一只耳环和四顶王冠中的一顶——窃贼在离开时似乎“掉落”了这顶王冠。 维耶纳发言人表示，“所有安全系统都已启动”，他坚称博物馆“没有出现故障”。 维耶纳宝藏收藏了 50 多件主要是黄金的物品，由考古学家何塞·玛丽亚·索勒 (Jose Maria Soler) 于 1963 年在干涸河床上的沉船中发现。 该藏品已在比耶纳以外的马德里、阿利坎特、东京和京都等城市展出，后来制作了两套复制品来展示该藏品，同时又不将其从维耶纳考古博物馆的装甲展示中带走。 这些文物的历史价值是无法估量的，尽管盗贼们可能很难在黑市上出售它们，因为他们从著名的展览中偷走了它们。市长表示，仅黄金一项就价值约 170 万欧元或 200 万美元。 据博物馆网站称，专业研究人员认为这是青铜时代最重要的金餐具收藏。它也代表了已知最早的例子......

title.en: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
title.zh: 斯雷布雷尼察幕后黑手：拉特科·姆拉迪奇去世，享年 84 岁

summary.en: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.

More than 30 years after the end of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina (1992-1995), Srebrenica remains emblematic of its brutality. And no one is more closely linked to the genocide that took place in the small town in eastern Bosnia than  Ratko Mladic , the former commander-in-chief of the Bosnian Serb army.

Although the United Nations had declared Srebrenica a "safe area," Bosnian Serb forces attacked the town. Within just a few days in July 1995, they expelled women and children, then killed more than 8,300 unarmed Muslim boys and men in the nearby village of Potocari — on Mladic's direct orders, according to the verdict handed down by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague 22 years later.

At the time, Srebrenica was the largest massacre in Europe since World War II . The ICTY classified it as genocide. Mladic was also held responsible for other war crimes beyond the Srebrenica genocide. Under his command, the years-long siege of Sarajevo began at the start of the war. The city was shelled for more than 40 months, killing around 11,000 people, including more than 1,600 children.

Mladic always claimed that he targeted only military objectives. But numerous reports and intercepted radio communications indicate that civilian facilities and residential areas were also deliberately attacked. Around 100,000 people were killed during the four-year war in Bosnia, while some 2.2 million were driven from their homes in cities and villages across the country, half of its total population at the time.

He was found responsible for some of the most serious war crimes and the genocide committed during the Bosnian War.

Mladic consistently denied any responsibility. He saw himself as an avenger of the Serbs for centuries of Ottoman rule in the Balkans, and viewed Bosnia's Muslims, who today call themselves Bosniaks, as direct descendants of the Turks. In front of his soldiers, he referred to them simply as "the Turks" and showed no empathy.

"Borders are always drawn with blood, and states are marked with graves," he is quoted as saying.

At the beginning of the Croatian War in June 1991, when Serbs living in Croatia rose up against the independence of the former Yugoslav republic with active support from Serbia, Mladic's role fundamentall changed. As a colonel in the Yugoslav army, he became commander of the 9th Corps in the Croatian city of Knin. His task was to organize Serb militias and support them in their fight against Croatian independence.

body.zh: 对许多人来说，拉特科·姆拉迪奇代表了波斯尼亚战争的恐怖。他因斯雷布雷尼察大屠杀和其他战争罪被判犯有种族灭绝罪。现在他在海牙拘留期间去世。 波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那战争（1992-1995）结束 30 多年后，斯雷布雷尼察仍然是其残暴的象征。没有人比波斯尼亚塞族军队前总司令拉特科·姆拉迪奇与发生在波斯尼亚东部小镇的种族灭绝事件关系更密切。 尽管联合国已宣布斯雷布雷尼察为“安全区”，但波斯尼亚塞族军队袭击了该镇。根据 22 年后海牙前南斯拉夫问题国际刑事法庭 (ICTY) 作出的判决，1995 年 7 月的短短几天内，他们驱逐了妇女和儿童，然后在附近的波托卡里村杀害了 8,300 多名手无寸铁的穆斯林男孩和男子——这是姆拉迪奇的直接命令。 当时的斯雷布雷尼察是二战以来欧洲最大规模的屠杀。前南问题国际法庭将其归类为种族灭绝。除斯雷布雷尼察种族灭绝事件外，姆拉迪奇还应对其他战争罪行负责。在他的指挥下，战争一开始，对萨拉热窝长达数年的围困就开始了。该市遭到长达 40 多个月的炮击，造成约 11,000 人死亡，其中包括 1,600 多名儿童。 姆拉迪奇始终声称他只针对军事目标。但大量报告和截获的无线电通讯表明，民用设施和住宅区也遭到蓄意袭击。波斯尼亚四年战争期间约有 10 万人被杀，全国各地城市和乡村约有 220 万人被赶出家园，占当时总人口的一半。 他被发现对波斯尼亚战争期间犯下的一些最严重的战争罪和种族灭绝负有责任。 姆拉迪奇始终否认负有任何责任。他将自己视为奥斯曼帝国在巴尔干地区统治几个世纪以来塞尔维亚人的复仇者，并将波斯尼亚的穆斯林（今天自称为波斯尼亚人）视为土耳其人的直系后裔。在他的士兵面前，他简单地称他们为“土耳其人”，并且没有表现出同情心。 引用他的话说：“边界总是用鲜血划定的，国家总是用坟墓来标记的。” 1991年6月克罗地亚战争爆发时，居住在克罗地亚的塞族人在塞尔维亚的积极支持下奋起反抗前南斯拉夫共和国的独立，姆拉迪奇的角色发生了根本性的变化。作为南斯拉夫军队的上校，他成为克罗地亚城市克宁的第九军团的指挥官。他的任务是组织塞尔维亚民兵并支持他们反对克罗地亚独立。 在姆拉迪奇的指挥下，克罗地亚城市...

title.en: Zambian opposition leader in police custody: state media
title.zh: 赞比亚反对派领导人被警方拘留：官方媒体

summary.en: Zambia's national broadcaster reports that Brian Mundubile, who wanted to challenge this month's presidential election results, and his running mate have surrendered to police and are being interviewed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 赞比亚国家广播公司报道称，想要挑战本月总统选举结果的布赖恩·蒙杜比莱(Brian Mundubile)和他的竞选搭档已向警方自首并正在接受采访。 据国家广播公司 ZNBC 周四报道，赞比亚反对派领导人、总统选举亚军布赖恩·蒙杜比勒 (Brian Mundubile) 已被警方拘留并接受讯问。 这是在一场有争议但基本和平的总统选举两周后发生的，当局宣布现任总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马获胜。 选举第二天，蒙杜比莱在警方突击搜查和逮捕后一直躲藏起来，称他计划在法庭上质疑选举结果，因为政府指控他犯有国家安全罪并密谋叛乱。 国家广播公司 ZNBC 报道称，蒙杜比莱和他的竞选搭档马克比·祖鲁“已被移交给警方，目前正在接受采访”。 警方发言人戈弗雷·奇拉比 (Godfrey Chilabi) 表示，两名反对派领导人正在接受执法人员的询问，他们的律师也在场。 奇拉比告诉 ZNBC，采访过程结束后将发表一份声明。 该广播公司报道称，两人在向警方自首之前一直在首都卢萨卡“受到联合国的保护”。 警方还表示，蒙杜比莱本周早些时候正在向一个“国际组织”寻求庇护，并表示该组织正在对反对派候选人及其竞选伙伴进行询问，试图在他们与“各种令人震惊的活动……有可能威胁或破坏国家安全”之间建立联系。 赞比亚于 8 月 13 日进行了投票，观察人士原本预计这次选举将为现任总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马 (Hakainde Hichilema) 的第二个任期提供相对明确的授权。 蒙杜比莱在选举之夜短暂宣布获胜，但希奇莱马呼吁人们等待计票和正式结果。 由于据称针对选举官员的袭击，计票过程一度短暂暂停。选举委员会最终发现希奇莱马赢得了约 60% 的选票，尽管蒙杜比莱的表现好于预期。 希奇莱马在投票前不久指控威胁国家安全的阴谋，投票后第二天，警方突袭了蒙杜比莱的家和其他反对派地点，逮捕了 11 人。前内阁部长穆托维·卡夫瓦亚 (Mutotwe Kafwaya) 在行动中的交火中被枪杀。蒙杜比勒躲了起来。 在希奇莱马之前统治赞比亚的统一与繁荣民族和解党 (NRPUP) 的领导人...

title.en: Collapsed glacier likely caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, scientists say
title.zh: 科学家表示，冰川崩塌可能导致尼泊尔-西藏地区发生毁灭性洪水

summary.en: Preliminary investigations by scientists have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Preliminary investigations have pointed to a collapsed glacier as the cause of the flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border, highlighting the issue of rapidly melting Himalayan ice, scientists have told the BBC.

Initial reports of an earthquake led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the flood that has killed at least 469 people.

However, the US Geological Survey then clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.

Dr Simon Cook, a glacier expert with the University of Dundee, told the BBC his team had detected that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - which is approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.

He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a northwesterly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

An analysis , external by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), an intergovernmental scientific institution, found there could have been "an ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-altitude area".

This caused a "large volume of ice and rock debris" to enter the Lende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi river, which in turn generated a sudden surge in the river carrying water, sediment and large boulders downstream.

The centre found that water levels in rivers downstream rose by between seven and nine metres within a span of 30 minutes, and several water monitoring stations were washed away or damaged.

Mike Searle, a professor of earth sciences at Oxford University, said that this whole process - from landslide to flood - could have taken hours or even days.

"The sheer wave of debris suggests there could have been a landslide first; the water built up, dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The topography of the area could have also exacerbated the flood. Searle pointed out that Langtang Lirung sits on the crest of the high Himalayas and there are "incredibly steep valleys" on both sides of the mountain, which could have funnelled the water at higher speeds.

Searle said that Langtang Lirung, like the rest of the Himalayas, has been slowly rising due to long-term tectonic movement, where one plate has been pushing another plate up. "It's like putting a jack under the car, and then jacking it up."

"As the mountain is rising, the glacier gets steeper and steeper, and it's inevitable that parts of it fall off."

body.zh: 科学家告诉英国广播公司，初步调查表明，尼泊尔和西藏边境山洪爆发的原因是冰川崩塌，这凸显了喜马拉雅冰川迅速融化的问题。 最初的地震报告让许多人相信地震引发了山体滑坡，进而引发了洪水，造成至少 469 人死亡。 然而，美国地质调查局随后澄清，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 根据美国地质勘探局的数据和分析该事件的科学家的数据，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级。 邓迪大学冰川专家西蒙·库克博士告诉英国广播公司，他的团队发现尼泊尔朗塘利龙峰附近的冰川下部已经崩塌，该峰位于洪水所在地以西约 15 公里（9 英里）处。 他估计冰川向西北方向崩塌，然后向下游向西移动。 政府间科学机构国际山地综合开发中心（ICIMOD）的一项外部分析发现，可能存在“源自高海拔地区的冰岩雪崩”。 这导致“大量冰和岩石碎片”进入博特科希河的支流伦德科拉河，进而导致河水突然激增，将水、沉积物和大石块带到下游。 该中心发现，下游河流水位在30分钟内上涨了7至9米，多个水监测站被冲毁或损坏。 牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，从山体滑坡到洪水的整个过程可能需要数小时甚至数天。 他告诉英国广播公司：“巨大的碎片浪潮表明，可能首先发生了山体滑坡；水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后爆发了一场巨大的洪水。” 该地区的地形也可能加剧洪水。塞尔指出，Langtang Lirung 坐落在喜马拉雅山的山顶，山的两侧都有“极其陡峭的山谷”，这可能会导致水以更高的速度流入。 塞尔表示，Langtang Lirung 与喜马拉雅山的其他地区一样，由于长期的构造运动，一个板块一直在推动另一个板块上升，一直在缓慢上升。 “这就像在汽车下面放一个千斤顶，然后把它顶起来。” “随着山的上升，冰川变得越来越陡，部分冰川脱落是不可避免的。” 但通常这些都是较小的块，会暂时堵塞河流，并且很容易......

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 我们对尼泊尔和西藏致命洪水的了解

summary.en: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Massive landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.

Search and rescue operations are continuing after Wednesday's disaster. Chinese state media has said there are significant casualties, while Nepalese officials describe "huge scale loss".

But rescuers are on edge because of the risk of further flooding. A lake of rising water has formed at a site along the border, and Chinese state media says it is at "high risk" of bursting its banks.

Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating flood.

However, the US Geological Survey has clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.

Debris flow from the collapse "caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream" the USGS said.

Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region. Scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events as rescue efforts continue.

Geologist Daniel Shugar – one of the first experts to suggest Wednesday's flash flooding event could have been caused by glacial activity – says glacial thinning inducted by global warming can increase the risk of landslides.

But it is still too early to definitively link the event to climate change, Shugar, who is based at the University of Calgary in Canada, tells the BBC.

Simon Cook, a geoscientist at the University of Dundee, says however, that climate change "could have an impact". Cook added that his team believed they had identified where the collapse had occured. He told the BBC that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.

He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a north-westerly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

He told the BBC "permafrost is partially holding some mountainsides together, this permafrost is warming and thawing and degrading so you are going to get more landslides".

Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

He told the BBC: "I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, (which) dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood."

title.en: Warning of fresh danger from rising lake water in Nepal – as it happened

summary.en: At least 165 people have died following a flash flood caused by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Hundreds of foreign nationals from various countries are among the missing. Eyewitnesses on the Tibetan side described trees and electricity poles being knocked down by the rapidly advancing floodwaters.

body.en: This live blog has now closed – but our coverage continues at a new blog here Eyewitness accounts have been emerging from the Tibetan side of the border , with a woman saying she was travelling from Gyirong town towards Nepal on Wednesday morning when her group encountered the flood about 4km from Gyirong port. “Trees and electricity poles had already been knocked down, and the flood water was bearing down on us. We didn’t dare turn around, so we could only reverse,” the woman, surnamed Fang, told Xiaoxiang Morning News . I was really scared. My whole body was trembling. Continue reading...

reflection.zh: 尼泊尔因冰川崩塌引发的毁灭性山洪，是对自然力量的巨大威力以及人类生命脆弱性的严峻提醒。大地本身在其现状下，因罪恶和败坏而呻吟，这一现实通过如此悲惨的事件触及我们所有人。在这些压倒性的损失时刻，我们被呼召与哀痛者一同哀哭，并持守未来复兴的盼望。

body.en: Risks rise of further flooding from rivers clogged by debris as rescue teams race to find more than 1,400 missing people Nepal flash flood – latest updates Nearly 1,400 missing, mostly tourists, and hundreds killed Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? Rescue teams and military helicopters are searching for hundreds of missing people along the mountainous Nepal-Tibet border after a huge torrent of water and mud swept through communities following a glacier collapse on Wednesday. More than 470 people were killed , authorities in Nepal and China said, and more than 1,400 were missing, including hundreds of foreign citizens and pilgrims. Nepal and China both warned of new flooding ⁠risks in the Himalayas because of two lakes that have developed along debris-choked rivers on either side of their border. Nepal’s disaster authority said water levels were rising in a lake formed by debris clogging a flooded site and ‌that it was at risk of bursting its banks. It did not name the specific site. Chinese authorities warned that a newly formed lake at the confluence of the Tsogyal and the Purupqiangzangbu rivers was overflowing and might burst. More than 500 foreign citizens were among 826 people missing in Nepal , police and tourism ⁠officials said. Among those unaccounted for were 177 from India, 90 from the US, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada. Chinese state media said at least 558 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, of whom at least 260 were foreign nationals. The Red Cross said about 93,000 people might have been affected , while assessments continued in hard-to-reach areas. It launched an emergency appeal for $31m to respond to the disaster. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said he ordered the release of $2m from the UN’s central emergency response fund to help with medical care, shelter and water. US president Donald Trump said the flooding was terrible to see , describing how “strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks”. Nepalese officials said dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40km of roads damaged , complicating search efforts. The Nepalese army had rescued more than 100 people by helicopter , an army spokesperson said. Army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project, he said. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for medical care . Rescuers found bodies in Nepal’s Chitwan district , hundreds of kilometres downstream from the hardest-hit areas. The Nepal Red Cross Society said the agency has shifted its focus from rescue to large-scale relief operations in the flood-hit districts. body.zh: 救援队竞相寻找 1,400 多名失踪人员，河流被碎片堵塞，进一步引发洪水的风险上升 尼泊尔山洪 - 最新动态 近 1,400 人失踪，其中大部分是游客，数百人死亡 视觉指南：致命洪水是如何展开的 告诉我们：您受到山洪的影响吗？周三冰川崩塌后，巨大的洪水和泥浆席卷了社区，救援队和军用直升机正在尼泊尔和西藏边境山区寻找数百名失踪人员。尼泊尔和中国当局表示，已有 470 多人死亡，1,400 多人失踪，其中包括数百名外国公民和朝圣者。尼泊尔和中国都警告喜马拉雅山将面临新的洪水风险，因为两国边境两侧的河流沿岸被泥石流淹没，形成了两个湖泊。尼泊尔灾害主管部门表示，由堵塞洪水地点的碎片形成的湖泊水位正在上升，面临决堤的危险。它没有透露具体站点的名称。中国当局警告称，措嘉河和普鲁羌藏布河交汇处新形成的湖泊正在泛滥，可能会决堤。警方和旅游官员称，尼泊尔失踪的 826 人中有 500 多名外国公民。下落不明者中有177人来自印度、90人来自美国、34人来自澳大利亚、33人来自英国和25人来自加拿大。中国官方媒体称，西藏边境一侧至少有 558 人失踪，其中至少 260 人是外国人。红十字会表示，大约 93,000 人可能受到影响，同时对难以到达的地区的评估仍在继续。它发出了 3100 万美元的紧急呼吁，以应对这场灾难。联合国人道主义事务负责人汤姆·弗莱彻表示，他下令从联合国中央应急基金中拨款 200 万美元，用于提供医疗、住房和供水方面的帮助。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，洪水的场面非常可怕，他描述了“坚固、建造精良的建筑物像牙签一样被摧毁”。尼泊尔官员表示，数十座桥梁被毁，近 40 公里的道路被毁，使搜寻工作变得更加复杂。尼泊尔军队发言人称，尼泊尔军队已使用直升机救出了100多人。他说，陆军小组还疏散了被困在与特里苏里水电项目有关的设施内的人员。数十名伤者被送往加德满都接受治疗。救援人员在距受灾最严重地区下游数百公里的尼泊尔奇旺地区发现了尸体。尼泊尔红十字会表示，该机构已将工作重点从救援工作转向洪水灾区的大规模救援行动。中国总理李强周四抵达吉隆，指导...

title.en: Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn
title.zh: 专家警告：气候危机可能导致尼泊尔等山区动荡不安

summary.en: A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse in the Himalayas has left at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing in the border regions of Nepal and Tibet. Experts warn that unusual heat is melting the ice bonds that hold glaciers in place, threatening millions as mountain geologies become increasingly unstable.
summary.zh: 喜马拉雅山脉冰川坍塌引发的灾难性山洪已导致尼泊尔和西藏边境地区至少360人死亡，1400人失踪。专家警告说，异常高温正在融化固定冰川的冰层纽带，随着山区地质结构日益不稳定，数百万人的生命受到威胁。

body.en: Unusual heat this year may have melted ice and thawed bonds that hold glaciers in place – leading to catastrophe Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates What caused the flash flood in Nepal and Tibet? The devastating flash flood that has ripped through the border communities of Nepal and Tibet has heightened fears that the climate crisis is destabilising the geology of mountain and polar regions, threatening millions of people. Satellite imagery suggests a glacier collapse high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the deadly torrent of mud, water and ice that tore along the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday. It swept away buildings and roads and left at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing. Continue reading...
body.zh: 今年异常炎热的天气可能会融化冰层并解冻固定冰川的债券，从而导致灾难 尼泊尔-西藏山洪 - 最新动态 是什么导致了尼泊尔和西藏的山洪？席卷尼泊尔和西藏边境社区的毁灭性山洪加剧了人们的担忧，即气候危机正在破坏山区和极地的地质稳定，威胁着数百万人。卫星图像显示，喜马拉雅山高处的冰川崩塌是周三博特科希河沿岸致命的泥浆、水和冰流的主要原因。它冲毁了建筑物和道路，造成至少 360 人死亡、1,400 人失踪。继续阅读...

As we mourn the hundreds lost in these flash floods, we recognize that creation is not a static backdrop but a living system that groans under the pressures of our era. In this instability, we are called to seek Yahweh's mercy for the...

title.en: Could new US sanctions tear China and Iran apart?
title.zh: 美国新制裁是否会导致中国和伊朗分裂？

summary.en: Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.

China has pushed back on what it called "illegal unilateral sanctions" after the US announced new measures earlier this week to cut off all potential sources of revenue to Iran.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday described the sanctions package as an "economic D-Day" against Tehran, and warned any economic engagement with the regime would "expose those responsible to the full reach" of US power.

China is Iran's top trade partner and provides a lifeline to Tehran mainly through oil purchases , but also with banking, technology and dual-use goods, which can be used both for civilian and military purposes.

When asked whether Chinese banks would be included in the new measures, Bessent warned that "no one was above the reach of US sanctions."

But with US President Donald Trump due to meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in September, Washington will need to be careful with any moves affecting China-Iran trade ties.

The initial US sanctions package stops short of targeting major Chinese banks. Instead, it focuses on 60 smaller entities, individuals, and vessels, both in mainland China and Hong Kong, that are part of the ecosystem supporting "illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil‑revenue generation networks."

China purchases up to 90% of Iranian oil exports, some of it through independent "teapot" refineries which end up rebranding the oil or using intermediaries to bypass US sanctions.

In May, China's Commerce Ministry ordered domestic businesses and teapot refineries to ignore US restrictions targeting several of these refineries. At the time, Bessent said China's Iran oil purchases amounted to "funding the largest state sponsor of terrorism."

On Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said cooperation between China and Iran "has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted."

China maintains a transactional relationship while framing instability in the Middle East as a failure of US policy . At the same time, Beijing also projects the image of a stable, responsible superpower , and avoids being lumped together with rogue states the US accuses it of supporting. Beijing also values its trade ties with Saudi Arabia and the UAE, prompting it to carefully balance its relationships to avoid alienating Iran's regional rivals.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the US sanctions package are likely to be on the agenda when Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attends the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)...
body.zh: 华盛顿对伊朗施加最大经济压力的战略因其缓和与中国政治紧张局势的愿望而受到削弱。 在美国本周早些时候宣布切断伊朗所有潜在收入来源的新措施后，中国反击了所谓的“非法单边制裁”。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周一将制裁计划描述为针对德黑兰的“经济诺曼底登陆”，并警告称，与该政权的任何经济接触都将“让责任人暴露在美国力量的全面影响之下”。 中国是伊朗最大的贸易伙伴，主要通过购买石油为德黑兰提供生命线，但也提供银行、技术和军民两用商品，这些商品可用于民用和军事目的。 当被问及中资银行是否会被纳入新措施时，贝森特警告称，“没有一家银行能够逃脱美国的制裁”。 但由于美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将于 9 月会见中国国家主席习近平，华盛顿需要谨慎对待任何影响中伊贸易关系的举动。 美国最初的制裁方案并未针对中国主要银行。相反，它重点关注中国大陆和香港的 60 个较小的实体、个人和船只，这些实体、个人和船只是支持“非法核和导弹技术采购、网络运营和石油创收网络”的生态系统的一部分。 中国购买伊朗出口石油的90%，其中一些是通过独立的“茶壶”炼油厂购买的，这些炼油厂最终重塑石油品牌或利用中间商绕过美国的制裁。 五月，中国商务部命令国内企业和茶壶炼油厂无视美国针对其中几家炼油厂的限制。当时，贝森特表示，中国购买伊朗石油相当于“为恐怖主义最大的国家资助者提供资金”。 周二，中国外交部发言人林健表示，中伊合作“始终在国际法框架内进行，不应受到干扰和破坏”。 中国维持着交易关系，同时将中东的不稳定视为美国政策的失败。与此同时，北京还塑造了一个稳定、负责任的超级大国的形象，避免与美国指责其支持的流氓国家混为一谈。北京还重视与沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋的贸易关系，促使其谨慎平衡关系，以避免疏远伊朗的地区竞争对手。 当伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安出席上海合作组织（SCO）时，中东持续的冲突和美国的制裁方案可能会被列入议程......

title.en: Nepal floods: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪灾：数百人死亡，一千多人失踪

summary.en: Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.
summary.zh: 救援队正在搜寻幸存者，此前一次冰川崩塌引发了尼泊尔和西藏的灾难性洪水。包括许多外国游客在内的数百人失踪。

body.en:
Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.

The death toll from catastrophic flash floods along the border between  Nepal  and Tibet has risen to at least 392, while more than 1,400 people were missing.

Rescue teams were searching for survivors on Thursday, a day after a glacial collapse sent a huge wall of mud and rock barreling through the Himalayan communities, sweeping away entire villages.

Even with rescue efforts underway, local authorities warned that a fresh disaster could occur as a lake that had formed due to the floodwaters was threatening to burst.

In Tibet, Chinese broadcaster CCTV reported 558 people missing in Gyirong county, including 260 foreigners. Three deaths had been confirmed there as of Thursday morning, with two villagers rescued.

The disaster struck Wednesday when a glacial collapse triggered a flood in the Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, in a corridor popular with trekkers and pilgrims connecting Kathmandu with Lhasa. 

Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters the death toll "will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered."

Neighboring India accounts for the largest proportion of missing foreign nationals. Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said that 288 Indians were unaccounted for in Nepal, while a further 200 were stranded in China awaiting rescue.

US officials said around 90 US citizens remained unaccounted for on Thursday. The US State Department said three have been rescued, but that it was not yet aware of any deaths among US citizens.

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal tourism board spokesperson, told the AP news agency that many of the missing were pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus. In addition to the Indian and US tourists, Sharma said 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians were also missing.

Reuters cited other police and tourism officials who put the missing tourists at 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.

China's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were unaccounted for. 

During a press conference in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said they were still verifying the breakdown of nationalities of the missing foreigners in Tibet, who were mostly tourists and pilgrims.

China authorities said they were in close communication ‌with Nepal on search and rescue efforts.

Chinese premier Li Qiang has traveled to affected areas in Tibet to view the emergency work, state media reported.

body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏冰川崩塌引发灾难性洪水后，救援队正在寻找幸存者。数百人失踪，其中包括许多外国游客。 尼泊尔和西藏边境的特大山洪造成的死亡人数已上升至至少 392 人，另有 1,400 多人失踪。 周四，救援队正在寻找幸存者，一天前，冰川崩塌导致一面巨大的泥土和岩石墙穿过喜马拉雅社区，席卷了整个村庄。 尽管救援工作正在进行，但地方当局警告称，由于洪水形成的湖泊有决堤的危险，可能会发生新的灾难。 在西藏，中国中央电视台报道吉隆县有 558 人失踪，其中包括 260 名外国人。截至周四上午，该地区已确认三人死亡，两名村民获救。 灾难于周三发生，冰川崩塌引发博特科希河支流伦德科拉河洪水泛滥，该河是连接加德满都和拉萨的徒步旅行者和朝圣者常去的走廊。 尼泊尔警方发言人阿比·纳拉扬·卡夫勒 (Abi Narayan Kafle) 告诉路透社，死亡人数“将会上升，因为我们已经恢复搜索，预计将找到更多尸体。” 邻国印度在失踪外国人中所占比例最大。印度外交部长苏杰生表示，有 288 名印度人在尼泊尔下落不明，另有 200 人滞留在中国等待救援。 美国官员表示，周四仍有约 90 名美国公民下落不明。美国国务院表示，三人已获救，但尚不清楚有美国公民死亡。 尼泊尔旅游局发言人苏尼尔·夏尔马 (Sunil Sharma) 告诉美联社，许多失踪者是前往西藏冈仁波齐峰的朝圣者，冈仁波齐峰是印度教徒的圣地。夏尔马说，除了印度和美国游客外，还有 34 名澳大利亚人、33 名英国人和 24 名加拿大人失踪。 路透社援引其他警方和旅游官员的话说，失踪的游客中有 34 名来自澳大利亚，33 名来自英国，25 名来自加拿大。 与此同时，中国外交部表示，近100名中国公民下落不明。 外交部发言人林健在北京举行的新闻发布会上表示，他们仍在核实西藏失踪外国人的国籍，这些人主要是游客和朝圣者。 中国当局表示，他们正在与尼泊尔就搜救工作保持密切沟通。 据官方媒体报道，中国总理李强已前往西藏受灾地区查看应急工作。 随着灾难的规模变得...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans under the weight of sin and disaster, as this devastating flood in Nepal and Tibet illustrates. In the midst of such overwhelming loss, we remember that creation itself awaits redemption, and we pray for comfort for those affected and for the eventual renewal of all things.
reflection.zh: 大地本身在罪恶和灾难的重压下呻吟，尼泊尔和西藏这场毁灭性的洪水便是明证。在如此巨大的损失面前，我们当铭记受造之物本身都在等待救赎，并祈求受灾者得到安慰，以及万物终将得到更新。

verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal floods climbs to 35
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
The Nepal Tourism Board says 35 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 273 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

That number had been 34 until the tourism board published an update Thursday afternoon.

Another 823 people, including 644 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

On Thursday afternoon, China's foreign minister said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were missing, revising down earlier reporting in Chinese state media that 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were missing in Gyirong Port, Tibet.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.

title.en: Deadly flash flood wipes away villages in Nepal, Tibet
title.zh: 致命的山洪摧毁了尼泊尔和西藏的村庄

summary.en: Dozens have died and hundreds were reported missing, including 341 foreign tourists. Rescue helicopters have been unable to land in affected areas due to high floodwaters.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Dozens have died and hundreds were reported missing, including 341 foreign tourists. Rescue helicopters have been unable to land in affected areas due to high floodwaters.

Dozens of people were confirmed dead and hundreds more are missing after a flash flood swept through remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday.

Nepali police said that authorities have recovered 157 bodies. Officers were "working to move families in flood-risk areas... to safer locations," police said.

"The pain and loss you have suffered is not small. But I want to assure you that you are not alone in this difficult time — the state is with you with all its means and resources," Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a statement.

"Please be patient. The government takes full responsibility for your rescue, treatment, food and shelter. In times of such a disaster, we all need to stand together."

In China, authorities said at least three have died, with 265 still missing, China's state broadcaster CCTV ‌said.

The floodwaters washed away villages, damaged bridges and destroyed electrical infrastructure on both sides of the Nepal-China border.

"There is devastation everywhere we look," ‌Tula ​Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa district, told Reuters.

"The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing."

At the same time, Chinese authorities also reported that a mudslide caused "major casualties" on the other side of the border in Tibet.

Nepal's Tourism Ministry said 403 travelers were reported missing for several hours after the floods struck. 

China's state news agency Xinhua reported Thursday that the number of missing people had increased to 558. State broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the missing people were foreigners.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Thursday that 34 Australians were missing following the flash flooding. 

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today," Albanese said.

A Nepali police spokesperson told Germany's DPA news agency that dozens of personnel were also missing.

"So far, we only have confirmation of 26 police personnel who remain missing in the flood," they said.

"We also have missing information of government revenue officials, hydropower workers among others. But we are still collecting the data."

Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said an earthquake triggered an avalanche in the Himalayas that then triggered flash floods in the valleys below.

Xinhua said a mudslide on the Nepali side of the mountains spread to Gyirong County in Tibet.

"Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out," said David Fisher, the Nepal head of the International Federation of Red...
body.zh: 数十人死亡，数百人失踪，其中包括 341 名外国游客。由于洪水泛滥，救援直升机无法降落在受影响地区。 周三，山洪席卷尼泊尔和西藏偏远山谷，已确认数十人死亡，数百人失踪。 尼泊尔警方表示，当局已找到 157 具尸体。警方表示，官员们正在“努力将洪水风险地区的家庭转移到更安全的地方”。 尼泊尔总理巴伦德拉·沙阿在一份声明中表示：“你们所遭受的痛苦和损失并不小。但我想向你们保证，在这个困难时期，你们并不孤单——国家将竭尽全力与你们同在。” “请耐心等待。政府对你们的救援、治疗、食物和住所负全部责任。在这样的灾难时刻，我们都需要站在一起。” 中国官方广播机构中央电视台称，中国当局表示至少有 3 人死亡，仍有 265 人失踪。 洪水冲毁了中尼边境两侧的村庄、桥梁和电力基础设施。 拉苏瓦地区的卫生工作者图拉·巴哈杜尔·BK (Tula Bahadur BK) 告诉路透社：“我们所看到的到处都是破坏。” “河边的定居点已被完全冲走。我自己的五个亲戚失踪了。” 与此同时，中国当局还报告称，边境另一边的西藏发生泥石流，造成“重大人员伤亡”。 尼泊尔旅游部表示，据报道，洪水袭击后数小时内有 403 名游客失踪。 中国官方通讯社新华社周四报道称，失踪人数已增至 558 人。官方电视台中央电视台报道称，其中 260 人是外国人。 澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞周四表示，山洪爆发后有 34 名澳大利亚人失踪。 阿尔巴内斯说：“我们的心与今天所有关心亲人的人同在。” 尼泊尔警方发言人告诉德国德新社，数十名人员也失踪。 他们说：“到目前为止，我们只确认了 26 名警察在洪水中失踪。” “我们还缺少政府税务官员、水电工人等的信息。但我们仍在收集数据。” 尼泊尔外交部长希西尔·卡纳尔表示，地震引发了喜马拉雅山雪崩，随后引发了下面山谷的山洪暴发。 新华社称，尼泊尔一侧的泥石流蔓延至西藏吉隆县。 国际红十字联合会尼泊尔负责人大卫·费舍尔说：“整个村庄和市场区域都被夷为平地。”

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国在关键矿产方面的竞争日益激烈，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能会在没有政策保护的情况下在几个月内开始。 洛伊研究所的分析发现，采矿最早可能在 2027 年开始，太平洋海底蕴藏着大量珍贵资源。 全球最大的两个经济体之间的竞争是由电池、武器系统和电网产生的需求驱动的。 研究表明，该地区各国在经济收益的承诺和生态系统、渔业、粮食安全、生计和文化遭受不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。 它认为，商业深海采矿国际治理框架的缺乏导致太平洋国家在没有国际商定保护的情况下进行谈判。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这也使得它们依赖于寻求海底采矿的公司起草的单独协议。 洛伊研究所的康纳·格雷厄姆写道：“对于陷入这场争夺关键矿产霸权的大国战争的太平洋岛国来说，这个经济提议很难拒绝。” “问题不在于太平洋国家不同意，而在于它们被迫与拥有更多资源、信息和法律能力的各方进行单独谈判，而旨在保护它们的国际框架已经陷入停滞。” 格雷厄姆表示，虽然澳大利亚尚未对太平洋深海采矿采取明确立场，但它拥有产生影响的地位、关系和机构存在。 这包括它是太平洋岛屿论坛的成员以及美国的长期盟友。 他说：“对尚未作为即将开始的活动条件的标准的承诺与其说是一项政策，不如说是一种弃权。” 包括澳大利亚在内的国家已开始签订关键矿物交易，这对许多新兴技术至关重要。 联邦政府宣布设立 12 亿美元的关键矿产战略储备，以确保对澳大利亚经济和国家安全至关重要的关键矿产的供应。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

As the report warns of mining commencing without adequate policy guardrails, the words of 1 Corinthians 10:23 remind us that while many actions may be permissible, not all are truly...

summary.en: One cohort accounted for almost half of these unintentional deaths, according to a new report.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article contains references to substance abuse and suicide.

Drug-induced deaths have hit a record high, with older Australians accounting for more than half of the fatalities.

Australia's Annual Overdose Report, released by the Penington Institute, documented 2,596 drug-induced deaths in 2024, with 80.5 per cent being from unintentional overdose.

Since 2008, more Australians have died from drug-induced deaths than road fatalities — with an average of 31 years lost per death.

"The data is quite confronting," Jake Dizard, director of research at the Penington Institute, told SBS News.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The report found that the median age of people dying from drug overdose is increasing.

For the first time, those aged between 50 and 59 accounted for almost half of all unintentional overdose deaths.

Dizard said it could be attributed to "an ageing large cohort of people who started using drugs in the 1990s and early 2000s".

"As that cohort has got older, they have become more vulnerable to drug-induced death because of the length of time that they have been using drugs and the accumulating sort of comorbidities," he said.

The report also noted that of the 428 drug-induced suicides, 39 per cent were people aged 60 and over.

Australian Alcohol and Other Drugs Council CEO Melanie Walker said the report confirms that overdose is not a "young people problem".

"It affects young people. It also affects older people. Overdose can be from illicit drug use, or it can be from prescription drug use."

The report also found that men accounted for 72.7 per cent of unintentional drug-induced deaths, people living in regional and rural areas had higher rates of death than those living in capital cities, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experienced higher rates of overdose.

In 2024, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experienced an overdose rate of 29.3 per 100,000 compared to 6.6 per 100,000 for non-Indigenous people.

Opioids were responsible for 42 per cent of all drug-induced deaths in 2024, with heroin-related deaths rising from 101 deaths in 2001 to 488 deaths in 2024.

Amphetamines were involved in 772 deaths, a record high for the drug, and cocaine was involved in 141 deaths. Benzodiazepines, alcohol and antidepressants also contributed to drug-induced deaths.

Dizard said that the use of prescription opioids, such as oxycodone, has declined since 2021 — a trend seen across "a number of categories of prescription drugs".

Cocaine was the only recorded drug that saw a decrease in the median age of people dying from overdose.

title.en: Exclusive: Memo reveals why NT Police were not charged over this death in custody
title.zh: 独家：备忘录揭示了为何北领地警方没有因这起拘留死亡事件受到指控

summary.en: Documents obtained by SBS News offer a new insight into the police response to the death in custody of Kumanjayi White.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
SBS News can reveal Northern Territory Police waited four months to send the NT's Director of Public Prosecutions (NTDPP) an 'opinion file' seeking advice after the death in custody of a 24-year-old Warlpiri man.

Known as Kumanjayi White for cultural reasons, the young man who also lived with disabilities died in May last year after he was restrained by two plain-clothes police officers in the confectionery aisle of an Alice Springs supermarket.

His death sparked nationwide protests over government inaction on Aboriginal deaths in custody, with protesters echoing calls by his family for an independent investigation.

White's family launched legal action against NT Police after it was announced the two officers involved would not be prosecuted in May — but discontinued the action earlier this month.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Now, an internal memo obtained by SBS News via a Freedom of Information (FOI) request offers an insight into the reasoning behind the NTDPP's decision not to prosecute.

The email obtained through FOI is dated 26 May 2026 and was sent by the then acting director of the NTDPP Patrick Williams to all NTDPP staff announcing the news that no charges would be laid over White's death.

"Shortly following your receipt of this email, it will become public knowledge that I have determined there are no reasonable prospects of securing a conviction on any charge arising out of his death on the basis of the evidence provided by police," Williams writes in the memo.

"For that reason, I have met with them on country this morning to inform them of the view that I have reached."

Williams goes on to explain the decision, noting that the department "may be the subject of some media criticism" as a result.

"That criticism may include questioning the integrity and independence of our office, noting the relationship between the NTDPP and NT Police Force," he writes.

It notes that a police opinion file was delivered in September 2025, four months after White's death.

At that time, acting NT police commissioner Martin Dole told media that investigators had "compiled a full and comprehensive brief of evidence".

But the internal memo obtained by SBS News reveals prosecutors had asked police to obtain an additional independent report into the use of force in White's arrest "within days" of receiving the opinion file in September.

It was later revealed by Dole that this 'use of force' report was conducted by Queensland Police.

The email also shows Williams sought advice from external interstate senior and junior counsel on whether the evidence provided by police was sufficient to warrant prosecution.
